info.name: OnBuy API Documentation v2
info.description:
The OnBuy API allows external applications to securely communicate with the OnBuy platform. It is based on the [REST architecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_state_transfer). With it, you can automate many tasks such as creating products, creating & updating listings and exporting orders. ## Getting Started The quickest way to get started with the OnBuy API is to click the **Run in Postman** button at the top of this page. All the endpoints documented here are available to run in the OnBuy Postman collection. Postman is a free tool to help developers run and debug API requests. Visit [https://www.getpostman.com/](https://www.getpostman.com/) to download. # Settings The [API settings page](https://seller.onbuy.com/inventory/integrations/onbuy-api/) can be found in your Seller Control Panel. It details the information you will need in order to connect to the API (e.g. the API URL) and displays your daily usage statistics. > If you do not have access to this page, please contact the OnBuy Seller Team by creating a ticket. ## Connection Details There are two sets of keys, Live and Test. You should use the Test keys when integrating with the API and switch to the Live Keys when you are ready to go live. Data created in test is stored separately in your account. The switch at the top right of your account can be used to switch between live and test data. Test data is currently available for products, listings and orders. ## Going Live Going live should be a simple case of switching to use your Live Keys. For product creation, you'll be unable to publish live products without first having live product creation enabled on your account. To get your account enabled for live product creation, you should first create the products using your live API keys. The products will then show in your Seller Control Panel under the 'Approve Products' [Approve Products Page](https://seller.onbuy.com/inventory/management/approve-products/) page. You will need to submit a support ticket and request that the OnBuy Support team review the products and approve your account. Once your account is approved you will be able to approve/publish your products to the live site. ## Usage Limits Each request type (POST, GET, PUT and DELETE) has daily and hourly usage limits. These should be high enough for the requirements of most sellers. If you find you are hitting the limits on a regular basis we may be able to increase them. Please contact the OnBuy Seller Team by creating a ticket. ## Requests With each request (with the exception of requestToken) you will need to send the access_token as an Authorization header. See the Auth section below for details of how to obtain the access token. Each endpoint specifies the request method to use. Allowed request methods are POST, GET, PUT, DELETE. As a general rule: - GET – Used when fetching items. - POST – Used when adding items. - PUT – Used when updating items. - DELETE – Used when removing items. How parameters are passed varies depending on the method and endpoint being called. Most POST and PUT requests are sent as JSON. ## Responses Our API uses standard HTTP response codes to inform users about the status of a request. Responses with 4xx & 5xx codes mostly specify errors related to missing keys, wrong authorisation or missing data, whilst 2xx response codes usually mean the request was successful.
CodeMessage / Error
200
OK Success
400
Bad Request Invalid request mostly due to wrong data.
401
Unauthorised Missing Secret or Consumer Key, Authentication Failed, Bad Token.
403
Forbidden Account does not have permission to the accessed method.
404
Not Found The requested resource was not found.
429
Too Many Requests Usage limit has been exceeded.
500
Internal Server Error Internal error. Please contact us.
Note: Unless otherwise specified, all dates are in UTC. ## Pagination Most browse methods support pagination. The results returned will contain a MetaData element with the following pagination fields: - limit – The limit applied to the result set. - offset – The limit applied to the result set. - total_rows – The total results available. Filters and Sorting fields sent in the request will also be included in the meta data. Different pages of results can be returned by changing the offset sent with the request. Some methods have a maximum limit value. ## Variables Throughout the documents are a number of variables, shown as {{name}}. These need to be replaced with appropriate values when calling the endpoint. The table below details some of the more common variables and examples of values to include:
VariableExample
{{access_token}}
This is the access token received when you authenticate with the API
{{site_id}}
The OnBuy Regional site id e.g. 2000 for the UK
{{seller_id}}
This is your unique seller ID. You can find this on the API page of the SCP
{{entity_id}}
This is you unique trading entity ID. You can find this on the API page of the SCP
{{category_id}}
You can obtain a list of categories by using the `/v2/categories` method
{{opc}}
A unique code we assign to each product
# Products The OnBuy.com marketplace has a single entry for each product from a manufacturer with potentially multiple sellers listing the same product. As a seller you can list an existing product with your own purchasing options or, if the product is not already in the OnBuy system, you can add it yourself giving the full manufacturer's description. # Creating a Product There are two stages to creating a product on OnBuy using the API. The diagrams below highlight the processes involved for each stage. ## Stage 1 We advise using the search function `GET /v2/products` to see if the product exists before trying to create a new one. If the product already exists the create listing method `POST /v2/products/{{onbuy_product_code}}/listings` can be used to add a new listing to it. > When using test API keys only products created in test are returned from the search and test listings can only be created on test products. If the product doesn’t already exist the create product method `POST /v2/products` can be used to add a new product. The product should be submitted as a JSON string. On receiving the product OnBuy will validate the supplied data to ensure it meets the criteria needed. If there is anything not right an error will be returned containing details on what needs to be fixed. An error will be returned if any required parameters are missing. If the product passes validation it is added to a queue to be created in the system. A queue ID is returned which can be used to check the status of the product creation. Multiple products can be queued for creation. ## Stage 2 The queues methods `GET /v2/queues` can be used to get the status of the product creation. Multiple queue ID’s can be checked at once. Each queue has a status. If the status returned is pending then the product is still waiting to be processed. While queued products are normally processed within a few minutes, but at busy times they can take longer. We would suggest polling the queue with batches of ID’s periodically. Once the queue has been processed the status will be changed to either Success if the product has been created or failed if there was a problem. When the status is failed an error message will be returned with details of what has failed. While most validation is done before the product is queued some checks can only be done during the save. An example is product images which often take time to download, so we only check the URL is valid initially, but process the images when the product is actually created. If the status is success the OPC of the created product will be returned. #### **Image Download Requirements** To successfully create products, we need to download images from your media service. If our requests to access these images are blocked, it prevents us from retrieving the necessary files, resulting in errors when the **queue_id** is called, such as: **Error downloading image** "https://cdn.onbuy.com/product/65b27dcc5e50f/990-990/large-dog-bed-in-tan-faux-fur-fleece-easipet.jpg" - Connection to the host URL has been refused This issue may arise due to blocking software or IP address filtering that prevents us from accessing the URLs. To resolve this, you will need to allowlist our IP addresses. Please ensure that the following IP addresses are allowlisted: - **34.142.64.77** - **34.142.18.212** - **35.246.83.100** - **34.105.246.78** By making these adjustments, you can ensure smooth product creation and avoid image download errors. # Creating Test Products Test products can be created via the API when using test API credentials. The live and test product database is shared. If the "product_code" (GTIN) you are using to create the product, exists against a live product, you will not be able to use it to create a test product. When using the GET Products: Search endpoint, if you are using your test credentials and sending the GTIN through to see if the product exists, it will not check to see if it exists as a live product. To do this, you'd need to use your live credentials. # Creating Test Orders Test orders can be created via the API Integration page within the SCP. Test orders can only be created against test products. Most data is filled in automatically but some of the parameters can be customised such as choosing the shipping options (if there are multiple options available) and adding products. Products should be added by SKU. It is also possible to set a custom email address for the order emails to be sent to. The seller primary email is used as the default value. # Partner Integrations If you're a technology business offering order fulfillment, inventory management, or similar solutions to online sellers, [reach out to us](https://www.onbuy.com/gb/sell/?talktoteam=open). You may qualify to have your integration added to our Seller Control Panel. If your integration is added, we'll provide you with a unique "Provider-Token" to include in the header of each API call. _Key: Provider-Token__Value: XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX_ This ensures that any seller using the integration has the correct integration enabled in the SCP. We can then lock the integration. If a seller attempts to use API keys obtained for a different integration, but we detect your partner header, we'll return an error: _the integration specified in the header doesn't match the integration defined in the API token._ # API Change Log

To connect to any API method, you first need to obtain your temporary secret access token. Please see the example to the right. Once you have obtained the access token, this should be set as one of the headers of your API request. Allowed request methods are POST, GET, PUT. Each endpoint highlights the method to use. The access token is only valid for 15 minutes, after which a new token will need to be requested. Note: Access tokens are linked to the IP address from which they were generated. This means the token is only valid for use from the same IP address. Any attempt to use the token from a different IP will result in a 401 response.
